title: Extra search changes some bullets, but does not establish a better readout
findings: Repeated swaps recover roles on 84/100 questions versus 81/100 for plain pooling, but adjusted intervals still include no improvement. Name recovery is unchanged; number recovery falls.
Pruning lowers the measured contradiction rate. Matched random deletion produces almost the same reduction, so the reconstruction rule has no demonstrated correctness advantage.
Prune-and-refill usually replaces bullets rather than adding them: only 1.3% of sites gain bullets. Reconstruction rises by 0.024 percentage points on average over plain pruning.
Independent reviews found both useful details and lost names, plus judge-label changes on surviving wording. These 469 previously inspected questions support exploratory conclusions.
slide_findings: Extra swaps add little reconstruction and no established quality gain.
Pruning and random deletion cut the measured contradiction rate similarly.
Refilling is rare. Judge-sensitive cases limit faithfulness claims.

method_findings.repeat_swap-n32: Role recovery rises from 81 to 84/100, while number recovery falls from 53 to 51/120. Adjusted parent intervals remain uncertain. Swaps change 12.1% of sites and add only 0.018 fit points on average.
method_findings.repeat_swap_then_prune_005-n32: Measured contradiction drops from 47.10% to 44.48%; random deletion reaches 44.51%. Mean bullets fall from 3.99 to 2.91. Guided pruning preserves more reconstruction, but has no established correctness advantage over shortening.
method_findings.bounded_prune_refill_005-n32: Only 1.3% of sites gain bullets. Role recovery rises from 80 to 83/100, but names fall from 39 to 38/100 and numbers from 55 to 53/120. Every adjusted parent interval includes zero.
method_findings.repeated_swaps_random_delete_match_005-n: Random deletion matches guided bullet counts at every site. Its contradiction rate is almost identical, despite losing more reconstruction. It also removes useful names and relations in inspected examples.

repeat_swap-n32.finding: Three swaps replace some ambiguous or Nora-owned test-result wording with a first fragment explicitly assigning the test results to Peter while Nora is anxious, making the father-as-worry-target inference more plausible. The native question changes from zero to one passing site relative to the plain-pool parent, but Original released Oracle Lens and best-N already passed elsewhere; this is not a gain over the original release. The proposal still invents several names and calls Peter unaware of results although the story has him mention the clinic call, so the association recovery is narrower than prose fidelity.

qualitative_review.judging_limit: Some judged gains/losses retain the same disputed quote or relation. Official scores are preserved; reviewed examples do not prove those labels reflect factual repairs.

resources.slide_summary: Cached samples and phrase vectors: no additional GPU inference. New Luna judging used about $2.03 in 195 seconds. Extra swaps and refills add only 0.018 and 0.024 reconstruction points on average over their parents.
